new_value: Investigated: the vector file was NEVER content-stale — regenerated output is byte-identical to committed tunnel_authorization.json (23 messages/26 POST/13 data-plane cases, deterministic seeded identities). Real root cause, two layers: (1) test/vectors was mode 0775 (group-writable) on this checkout, so atomic_json._open_owned_directory raised 'parent directory is unsafe'; (2) the --check path caught that RuntimeError and reported it as a FALSE 'out-of-date' verdict (except (FileNotFoundError, RuntimeError): current=None conflated unsafe-dir with missing file). Environment fixed (chmod 755, host-local, untracked) and the checker made honest: generate_tunnel_authorization.py main() now separates FileNotFoundError (missing file -> 'out-of-date', exit 1, pre-existing semantics) from OSError/RuntimeError ('cannot safely read <name>: <error>', exit 2, loud). All three paths verified live: healthy=0, unsafe=2 with honest message, missing=1. Gateway suite 250/250 green (generator_is_fresh test now passes); ruff clean. wrong_algorithm negative case (authorizations[9], a10139ffff) untouched and preserved. Reviewer security note folded in: handler widened from RuntimeError to (OSError, RuntimeError) so PermissionError-class parent-dir failures also get the exit-2 contract; FileNotFoundError listed first so missing-file semantics are unchanged. Follow-up bead filed: the same masking pattern exists in 17 sibling generators (mechanical sweep).
